newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan group, China banking officials to hold forum.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan group, China banking officials to hold forum.

text.p: A Chinese banking delegation will start a two-day visit to Taiwan for a meeting to discuss the banking systems in both the countries and financial relations with Hong Kong after 1997, event sponsors said on Monday.
They said the 26-person delegation, including officials from the People's Bank of China, will meet with Taiwanese business leaders in a private forum.

The event is sponsored by the privately-funded Taipei Foundation of Finance. The mainland delegation is not scheduled to meet Taiwan government officials, according to an itinerary issued by the foundation.

Taiwan and China have been political rivals since they split after a civil war in 1949. Taiwan has banned all direct official contact with communist China but economic ties have flourished between the two sides despite a frosty political impasse.
Taiwan's economics ministry said in September it was easing rules to allow more visits from China's business circles.
Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have poured more than US$20 billion worth of indirect investments into China since the late 1980s.

In August, Taiwan tycoon Kao Ching-yung led nearly 80 Taiwan business leaders and politicians to Beijing to meet President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders in China. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
